title: 1. Concept of Natural Vegetation and Biomes

blocks.content: Ecological succession represents the gradual and orderly process of ecosystem development through distinct seral stages.

rows: Bare rock, lava flows, sand dunes (No soil)
Deforested area, burned forest, flooded land (Soil present)
Extremely slow (hundreds to thousands of years)
Relatively rapid (decades to a few centuries)

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Ecological succession is the predictable, directional process of change in species composition over time.
Primary succession initiates on newly formed, sterile substrates lacking pre-existing organic soil.
Secondary succession occurs following disturbances in areas where soil and organic matter remain intact.
The developmental intermediate stages are referred to as seral communities or seres.
The ultimate stable, self-perpetuating end-state in equilibrium with the climate is the climax community.
Primary vs. Secondary Succession: Secondary succession proceeds significantly faster because soil substrate is already present.
Pioneer Species Identification: Lichens and mosses serve as pioneer species in Xerarch (dry) succession, whereas Phytoplankton pioneer Hydrarch (aquatic) succession.
Autogenic vs. Allogenic Succession: Autogenic succession is driven by biotic components of the ecosystem, while Allogenic succession is driven by external abiotic forces.
